content: In NLP, we often get such invariance for free, e.g., for a word-level model, most of the perturbations produced by our character-level adversary lead to an UNK at its input. If the model is robust to the presence of these UNK tokens, there is little room for an adversary to manipulate it. Character-level models, on the other hand, despite their superior performance in many tasks, do not enjoy such invariance. This characteristic invariance could be exploited by an attacker. Thus, to limit the number of different inputs to the classifier, we wish to reduce the number of distinct word recognition outputs that an attacker can induce, not just the number of words on which the model is “fooled”. We denote this property of a model as its sensitivity.
